_README: Quotes chosen BY A HUMAN from the meeting videos. This file is
maintainer-owned in exactly the way rubric.md is: nothing here is picked,
written, or ranked by a model, and render.py only lays out what it finds.
'items' holds one quote per agenda item, keyed by the namespaced item
number merge.py produces. 'speakers' holds a short excerpt for one
public-comment speaker, keyed by meeting numberdate and then by the
speaker's start_seconds in out/recap-pubcomment-<period>.json — the same
anchor the timestamp link uses, so an excerpt can never drift onto the
wrong speaker. Keep speaker excerpts under ten words: they sit on the same
line as the timestamp, and the point is to say what the person ASKED THE
BOARD TO DO, not to summarize their two minutes.
All text is the meeting's AUTOMATIC CAPTIONS, which are an ASR guess and
not a certified transcript — which is why everything renders with its
timestamp link and says where it came from. The reader verifies it by
listening. Use an ellipsis for anything elided and square brackets for a
corrected caption mangling (a speaker excerpt records its own fix in
this README rather than a 'note' field); note any other departure, so the
edit is on the record rather than invisible.
'speaker' is only ever filled in when the video itself establishes who is
talking — a self-identification, or the chair or another member naming
them on the record. A caption SPELLING is not evidence (see CLAUDE.md:
Chen comes through as Chem, Chan and 'Jen Charlton'). Leave it out rather
than guess. Public-comment speakers are never named at all: the recap
counts them and links them, and that is the whole of it.
RESOLVED (was PENDING): the eleventh speaker (34:25) is now counted.

public_comment_period without pubcomment.extend_to_next_item, so every

Speaker 3 (1056) is deliberately excerpt-less — nothing he said stands up
as a short quote, and a blank there is honest; the timestamp still works.
The keys here are ANCHORS, and re-running classify_speakers moves them a
few seconds when its prompt changes. The August 2026 keys were re-mapped
once, on 2026-08-25, when the subtopic field was added: each moved 1-13s,
in order, one-to-one. One excerpt was dropped in that pass — 2069, 'put a
[three-letter] identifier ahead of the message' — because no speaker is
placed there any more. Re-key it by hand if that speaker is real.
'votes' names the members a roll call recorded as ABSENT or ABSTAINING,
keyed by the same namespaced item number. This is the one place a member's
name reaches the page, and it is here — in the human's file — because the
captions cannot support it: votes.py reads the roll call off an ASR track
that spells Cavazos as Kvassos, Kabaso and Vasquez. A name goes in only
after a person has checked the caption roll call against the board's real
roster and written down how they did it in 'note'. Leave the block out and
the tally prints '(1 absent)', which is always true.

_README: Where an agenda item actually STARTS in a meeting's recording, when
the segmenter got it wrong. Keyed by the namespaced item number, then
by meeting numberdate; the value is 'MM:SS', 'H:MM:SS' or bare
seconds. render._watch_line uses it for that meeting's link and falls
back to the segmenter's own anchor when there is no entry.
This is a DISPLAY override, not a re-measurement: the minutes that
rank items still come from segmentation and are unaffected. Nothing
on the page claims a duration any more, so an override moves one
link and nothing else.
A meeting's value may instead be an OBJECT of label -> timestamp:
"20260804": {"Presentation": "7:20", "Discussion": "14:18"}
Each entry renders as its own '[Watch <label>]' link, in file order,
with no 'Watch this agenda item:' prefix. The label is a person's word
for what that timestamp points at — allowed here for the same reason a
quote or an absentee name is: a human watched and wrote it down. When
ANY meeting for an item uses the object form the item is explicit-only:
a meeting with no entry, or an entry set to null (meaning 'a person
checked and there is nothing here'), emits no link.
6.01: saved anchor 28:11 landed in the previous item's tail; a person
read the presentation at 28:37 and the board discussion at 52:20 off
the Aug 4 work session. The Aug 18 anchor (48:54) was Mr. Hosang on
unrelated matters — set to null. 8.07's saved anchor was 1:22:18, the
VOTE; the item was taken up at 7:20 as 5.01 (presentation) with board
discussion at 14:18 and voted the same evening as 8.07 (see CLAUDE.md).
A person's replacement wording for an off-agenda public-comment topic,
keyed by the classifier's OWN label (case-insensitive); the value is
what the recap prints instead. This is the one place the model's topic
phrasing can be overruled by hand, and it is reviewed the same way the
label itself is (out/pubcomment-review-<numberdate>.md).
DISPLAY ONLY: the review file still shows the classifier's own label
over the captions it was assigned from, because that is what has to be
checked against the source. This block only changes the recap page.
'school renaming request' -> 'Renaming James Blair Middle School': the
classifier's Jan-Aug wording drifted; the single Aug 18 speaker
(30:34) asked to rename James Blair Middle School by name.
